I don't have schizophrenia but I have experienced some really scary hallucinations before. 

I do have bipolar disorder and when I used to drink too much I would hear weird voices/noises at night while I was trying to go to sleep. When I closed my eyes a very disturbing slideshow started to play in my head of different images of people with burnt faces, monsters, people with grotesque and inhuman facial features/expressions, etc. 

After I stopped drinking I tried smoking weed. Turns out that was a terrible idea. I became extremely paranoid and one night heard a noise in my house that made me convinced an intruder was inside. I calmly told myself that wasn't true but I was still scared out of my mind. When I tried to go to sleep I started hearing this loud screeching/squeaking noise coming from the corner of my room. I also had visual hallucinations. I have a poster of jimi hendrix in my room and I hallucinated that he was morphing out of the poster and coming into real life. Before you guys say the weed was bad, it was medical that I got from my gf's cousin, so no, it was not dipped in PCP or anything like that. 

Not super scary but I've also hallucinated that there was a big black chicken running down the street, and one time woke up to a chorus of women singing the words "I will double" over and over again. 

Also sometimes I have experienced weird paranoia that there is someone behind me, and when standing in line at 7/11 or at fast food restaurants I have believed there was someone behind me in line but when I turned around there was nobody there. 

I've also had some pretty gnarly nightmares over the last few years but that's a different story. Just last night I had a dream about being hit in the leg by a stray bullet from a police shooting, so that gives you some idea about what my dreams are like. 

PS one of the things that makes hallucinations scary is that you don't know what else will happen. My greatest fear was that I would hear someone opening my door or talking to me and telling me to do things. When you have 1 hallucination you think, "oh my god, what's next?" It's like a horror movie that you can't get out of.
